headline: Fears of AI curbs after Democrats' sweep sink the Nasdaq 5.5 percent; Kospi trips circuit breaker
subhead: The S&P 500 fell 4.4 percent to 7,353.7 and the VIX jumped 69.7 percent as Micron lost 17.5 percent, AMD 17.3 and Nvidia 9.3; Samsung fell 10.0 percent in Seoul.

us.text: The S&P 500 fell 4.4 percent to 7,353.7, the Nasdaq 5.5 percent and the Dow 3.4 percent on fears Democrats curb AI spending.
Chips led losses after top Democrats urged a data center moratorium: Micron fell 17.5 percent, AMD 17.3 and Nvidia 9.3.
October payrolls due Friday are forecast near 65,000 after September's 29,000, one of the last inputs before the Fed's 9 December decision.

india.text: Nifty jumped to 24,536.6 on 5 November on the US midterm result and a crude slump; the price feed still shows the 4 November close of 23,960.6.
Foreign investors bought a net 7,284 crore rupees of shares on 4 November while domestic institutions sold a net 3,712 crore.
The rupee settled at 94.46 per dollar on 5 November as gains in local stocks and softer crude limited losses.

global.text: The Kospi tripped a circuit breaker Friday and is down 13.4 percent from its 4 November close; Samsung Electronics fell 10.0 percent.
Europe faded early gains on 5 November: the STOXX 600 slipped 0.38 percent to 654.87 as technology shares fell 3.2 percent.
Brent rose 4.7 percent to 99.03 dollars after tanker attacks near Hormuz, rebounding from its lowest settlement since 31 August.

weekly.narrative: The week turned on whether AI spending pays: Alphabet had its worst day on record after negative free cash flow, ServiceNow and Caterpillar sank on guidance, and Intel and Amazon closed the week with a broad tech sell-off that left the Nasdaq down 2.0 percent and the S&P 500 down 0.6 percent. The Fed held rates on 28 October with two officials favouring a hike, and with oil lifted by fresh Hormuz attacks, rate fears hit metals hardest: gold lost 2.7 percent on the week to near a 52 week low and silver 8.6 percent. India moved the other way, with the Nifty back above 23,000 on IT and pharma buying, Trent jumping on results and foreign investors turning net buyers on Friday. Crypto absorbed a 6.3 billion dollar Binance hack, leaving Bitcoin down 4.8 percent in the week to 30 October. Next week brings Apple results on 2 November, the US midterm elections on 3 November, the Bank of England on 5 November and US payrolls on 6 November.
